title: Postmortem: BGP route flap on secondary transit provider
summary: edge-gw-02 announced and withdrew the primary prefix 14 times in 10 minutes during provider maintenance. BFD failed traffic to the primary transit in under 2 seconds each time; no user-visible impact.
contributing_factors: Maintenance window was not filed against the peering calendar
Route flap damping was disabled on the secondary session

incident.title: BGP route flap on secondary transit provider edge-gw-02

action_items.description: Enable route-flap damping on both transit sessions

title: Postmortem: auth-session-cache miss rate on redis-auth-prod
summary: An eviction-policy change flipped redis-auth-prod from allkeys-lru to volatile-ttl, and sessions without a TTL set were evicted first. Miss rate peaked at 12.6%, doubling origin reads for 22 minutes.
contributing_factors: Eviction policy drifted from the config store baseline
No alert on cache hit ratio below 95%

action_items.description: Enforce allkeys-lru via config-store drift detection
Alert when session-cache hit ratio drops under 95%

title: Postmortem: kafka consumer-lag warning on billing-events
summary: The billing-ledger-workers consumer group fell 48,210 messages behind after a partition rebalance doubled assignment asymmetry. Batch delay peaked at ~3 minutes; no billing events were dropped.
contributing_factors: Rebalance left one worker with 4 of 6 partitions

incident.title: Kafka consumer-lag warning on billing-events queue backlog > 45,000 msgs

action_items.description: Add per-partition lag alert at 20k sustained 10m

title: Postmortem: latency spike p99 > 1850ms (database connection pool exhaustion)
summary: The Postgres primary pool saturated at 498/500 leases (99.6%) after a slow migrations query leaked synchronous checkout connections. Edge ingress pods dropped threads and p99 latency breached 1850ms for 11 minutes until the leaked leases were reaped. Executive summary: ~41,200 users saw checkout errors peaking at 18.4%; no billing data was lost.
contributing_factors: Leaked connections held leases with no idle reaping (statement timeout absent)
Pool saturation alert fired only at 100%, leaving no ramp warning
The migrations runner shares the checkout connection pool

incident.title: Latency Spike p99 > 1850ms (Database connection pool exhaustion)

action_items.description: Add a 5s statement timeout to every pooled checkout query
Move the migrations runner onto a dedicated pool
Alert on pool lease saturation at 80% with a 5-minute ramp

title: Postmortem: cart service outage during flash sale
summary: A flash-sale traffic spike exhausted the cart service database connection pool. The pool had no statement timeout, so a slow pricing query held connections until every worker starved. The incident ran 38 minutes: 4 to ack, 34 to roll back the pricing query and drain the pool.
contributing_factors: Pricing query shipped without a statement timeout
Connection pool sized for normal traffic, not sale traffic
No load test in CI for the flash-sale profile

incident.title: Cart service outage during flash sale

action_items.description: Add a 5s statement timeout to every cart-service query
Raise pool ceiling and add saturation alerting at 80%
Add a flash-sale load profile to the CI pipeline

title: Postmortem: SSO login throttling misconfiguration
summary: A config migration reset the SSO throttle window from 10 attempts to 2, locking out frequent SSO users for ~2 hours until the hotfix shipped.
contributing_factors: Throttle defaults lived in code, not in the config store
Config migration lacked a regression test

incident.title: Login throttling misconfigured for SSO users

action_items.description: Move throttle defaults into the config store
Add a regression test covering config migrations
